title: Clarify 429 semantics, add retry guidance header, and harden stream framing for function/tool calls
author: Chen Li
description: Motivation: customers and SDKs have reported ambiguous retry behavior when receiving 429s from the OpenAI-compat shim and occasional stream desyncs during tool/function calls. This PR splits rate-limit semantics into explicit categories, introduces a machine-readable retry advice header, and tightens streaming frame checks to reduce malformed event propagation. Summary of changes: 1) 429 subclassing: responses now include an error.code of either 'rate_limit.client' or 'rate_limit.transient' depending on whether the caller exceeded a quota window vs system overload. 2) New header X-Redwood-Retry-Advice: structured (stringified JSON) object with keys retry_after_seconds, backoff_strategy and idempotency_recommendation. This provides deterministic guidance for SDKs and proxies instead of overloading Retry-After semantics. 3) Idempotency: tool/function call handler now validates and echoes the incoming Idempotency-Key; when a request is non-idempotent and a transient 429 is issued, the body includes 'retryable': true/false in the standardized error payload. 4) Streaming: strengthened frame boundaries, introduced sequence numbers for function-tool frames, and explicit stream-termination frames that include final error code mapping to the standardized schema. 5) Backwards compatibility: when clients do not understand X-Redwood-Retry-Advice, Retry-After is still set to a coarse integer; existing error fields remain present. 6) Observatory: added telemetry for 429 subclass counts, header adoption, and stream-framing errors to the console dashboards. Compatibility risks: SDKs that previously parsed ambiguous Retry-After headers may adopt the new guidance header; we will coordinate rollout with SDK teams. Rollout plan: staggered feature-flag rollout starting with hosted API then Dedicated, with a fallback to legacy behavior via config flag. Tests and validation: unit tests added for header generation and stream framing; e2e replay tests against real traffic samples; canary in perf-canary fleet for 48h. Related Linear items: ENG-1987, ENG-2114.

reviews: Amina Patel: I like the clear separation of transient vs client 429s. Can we ensure nginx/load-balancer doesn't rewrite the new header?
Chen Li: We added header passthrough tests and a fallback to Retry-After for BEs that strip custom headers.
Diego Morales: Stream seq numbers make sense. Please add a guard in the parser to drop frames where seq < last_seen to avoid replays.
Chen Li: Added seq guard and a small metric for dropped-frames; updated tests.
release_notes: Clarifies 429 semantics by splitting client vs transient rate limits, introduces X-Redwood-Retry-Advice header for deterministic retry guidance, strengthens stream framing for function/tool calls, and adds telemetry for adoption and errors.
notes_for_sdk_teams: SDKs should prefer X-Redwood-Retry-Advice when present. For older deployments, continue to honor Retry-After. Python and Typescript SDK adapters have been updated in this PR and will be released in the next patch.
rollout_strategy: feature-flagged rollout: hosted API -> dedicated staging -> dedicated prod -> private with opt-in. Fallback to legacy mode available via config.redwood.legacy_retry_headers = true.
qa_summary: Unit and integration tests added. E2E replay tests validated against samples from Feb 2026 incidents. Canary observed 0.6% reduction in client-retry storms and 72% fewer stream-desync errors in first 48h.
security_considerations: No new secrets. Custom header is informational only; ensure no sensitive data included in X-Redwood-Retry-Advice. Reviewed by security team on 2026-02-20.
observability_changes: New metrics: openai_compat.429_subtype{type}, openai_compat.retry_advice_sent, stream.frame_dropped_count. Dashboards updated in console.
migration_guide: Clients: switch to X-Redwood-Retry-Advice when available. For idempotency, always send Idempotency-Key for tool/function calls; SDKs will automatically echo and persist keys to avoid double-exec. See docs/api/retry_and_errors.md.
